day.reading: sequential specific mutations are vanishingly improbable

critic.reading: the same post says the single-specific-path model is not the real count; the chain is not a model of evolution
critic.number: none: the critic position rejects the model rather than offering another count; the back-calculation (0.9727, 1,080,000) is the post's own

notes: 300,000^500 = 3.636e2738 (exact integer, 2,739 digits) reproduces '3.6 x 10^2738 to 1'; the chance is 2.750e-2739 against the printed 2.7 (truncated). For exactly 1e-6 overall the step must succeed with 0.972747, which needs 1,080,778 candidate beneficial mutations per step; Day's 0.9727 and 1,080,000 reproduce to 0.07%. All of it assumes one specific path, which the post itself says cannot be assumed.
